description: Playing a scene: input to expected output. Every runtime must produce the same walk.

suites.description: Three dialogs in a row, each leaving by out.
An option id IS its exit port. There is no out on a choice.

cases.description: C3 exists on no wire: a dead end, which is the drawing, not an error.

suites.description: No portPerCase: every case must hold. out when they do, default when not.
The false exit of an if-style condition is `default`. v1 called it `false`.
portPerCase: the FIRST case that holds takes its own port.
A case with no `when` is always true, and shadows every case below it.
An action leaves by then, or by catch when a call failed.
A failure with no catch wired carries on through then.
The actor port is the CARD ID, with out as the else exit.

cases.description: A card the block does not cite has no port; out is the else exit.

suites.description: Options are tagged, never removed. The game filters.
The reserved `choice` dictionary reads a past answer of THIS scene.
A note is never dispatched; the walk steps over it.
A note wired back on itself ends the flow instead of overflowing the stack.
A choice wired back to itself, left on the second pass.
The first non-async target is the main flow; the rest run in parallel.
Tests chain left to right with NO precedence.
One true on an OR chain is enough.
An AND chain with one false is false.
DIALOG-001 exists in both scenes. A block is (scene, id), nothing else.
A scene answers to its path AND to the id that survives a rename.
waitForBlocks parks the MAIN flow too, not only a parallel track.

cases.description: DIALOG-404 is not in the scene, so DIALOG-002 is never even dispatched.

suites.description: A wait on a block already visited lets the flow through at once.

text.en: waits for the one behind it

suites.description: The same rule on a parallel track: an unreachable wait parks the branch.
A port whose every target is isAsync: the branches play, and the main flow ending is not the scene ending.
Two non-async targets on one port: the second is walked after the first, not beside it.
A branch and everything under it finish before its sibling starts.
An isAsync target runs beside; the non-async ones stay this track's, in order.
